subject: Realtime inference fragmentation and intermittent WS timeouts
messages:
From: Tom Hart <tom.hart@brightline.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [Brightline] Realtime fragmentation & intermittent WS timeouts

Hi Neha,

We're seeing a pretty bad regression from ~08:40 PT this morning across our realtime fleet talking to Redwood. Symptoms: token streaming is fragmenting (clients receive many tiny chunks instead of steady tokens), WebSocket connections intermittently time out, and overall throughput has dropped ~40%. Error rate (HTTP 5xx + WS disconnects) is up ~3.2% over the last hour.

Observed impacts: our user-facing chat sessions stutter (partial lines displayed), and a subset of clients get a final socket close with code 1006. This is affecting ~12% of our sessions in us-west region (sampled). We've attached a short trace and a small capture of the WS conversation as support_trace_0411.txt.

Quick details you might need:
- Example correlation id: cb9f3a27-8a5f-4b2c-9d2a-0f44a1e2d501
- Model endpoint: rwd/gpt-3.5-rt-prod:v13 (we haven't changed client configs)
- Client SDK: brightline-js v2.4.1 using chunked-transfer and WS streaming

Can someone from your side confirm whether there are known runtime changes or infra events this morning? This is customer-impacting for us.

--
Tom Hart
Head of Platform, Brightline
Tom.Hart@brightline.ai

Attachments: support_trace_0411.txt (5KB)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: [Brightline] Realtime fragmentation & intermittent WS timeouts

Tom — thanks for the heads up and the trace. We see the correlation id in our ingress logs. I am escalating internally and copying runtime on-call (Dev) + SRE lead (Rishi).

Immediate triage notes:
- We're checking host-level metrics and recent deploys; nothing shows as a platform-wide deploy at 08:40 PT but a smaller routing change rolled at 07:58 PT to a subset of us-west nodes.
- For mitigation we recommend (a) forcing your clients to fall back to short-polling until we stabilize OR (b) toggling client keepalive to 15s while we investigate.

I've attached the trace you provided into our ticket and included a short excerpt of the logs. We'll follow up with a technical analysis within 45 minutes.

Next steps (we'll own):
1) Dev and SRE will analyze the dump + kernel logs and confirm if this is network/proxy chunking or runtime kernel behavior.
2) If it's proxy-level fragmentation, we can push a hotfix to disable chunk coalescing in the edge proxy for the affected pool.
3) If it's model-side, we'll switch affected customer traffic to the last-known-good model variant and route to alternate pool.

Appreciate the data you sent — keep the traces coming if you see more ids.

--
Neha Kapoor
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, Tom Hart <tom.hart@brightline.ai>
Date: 2026-04-11T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Brightline] Realtime fragmentation & intermittent WS timeouts

Thanks Neha — I pulled the sample_ws_dump_0411.log and the ingress traces. Initial read: this looks like chunk fragmentation + reassembly failures between our edge proxy pool and backend runtime on a subset of nodes. A few specific signals:

- Reassembly timeouts: we see repeated small TCP writes from the proxy (<= 512 bytes) with missing FIN boundaries, causing our read-loop to return early and the runtime to emit tiny "delta" chunks.
- WS ping/pong gaps: backend is not receiving pongs within the expected interval due to delayed thread scheduling on certain hosts (CPU steal observed in host metrics).
- Correlated error pattern with routing change at 07:58 PT that moved ~22% of Brightline traffic to a new edge pool.

Short mitigations I recommend we can apply within 30-60 minutes:
1) Disable chunked buffering on the edge proxy for the affected pool (command: ./edgectl set chunk_buffering=false --pool us-west-3-hotfix).
2) Increase websocket keepalive/send interval from 10s -> 15s and bump server-side read timeout to 65s.
3) Enable legacy_chunk_coalescing in runtime for that pool (runtime flag: --enable-legacy-chunk-coalesce) as a temporary guard.
4) If host CPU steal persists, shift load off the three hosts showing >25% steal to an alternate pool and reroute fresh connections.

If these steps don't bring error rate below 0.5% within 30 minutes we'll plan a controlled rollback of the 07:58 routing change and fail traffic back to prior pool.

I've attached the WS dump (sample_ws_dump_0411.log) with inline markers where the reassembly gaps occur.

- Dev

Subject: Escalation: Brightline realtime fragmentation affecting throughput and error rates — exec sync

Marcus — looping you in. Brightline (BR-5821), a strategic mid-market account, reported a realtime degradation starting 08:40 PT this morning. Impact summary:

- Customer-visible: chat sessions show token fragmentation and stuttering; ~12% session impact in sampled us-west fleet; throughput down ~40% for affected customers.
- Error metrics: integrated error rate rose to 3.2% (5xx + WS disconnects), currently trending down to ~1.1% after mitigations but not stable.

What we did so far:
- On-call runtime applied temporary mitigations (edge chunk_buffering disabled, websocket keepalive increased, enabled legacy chunk coalescing for affected pool).
- SRE rebalanced load away from hosts showing CPU steal; error-rate improved from 3.2% -> 1.1% in 90 minutes.
- We collected traces and WS dumps; attachments: sample_ws_dump_0411.log and a short mitigation playbook (proposed_mitigation_playbook.pdf).

Asks for exec:
1) We may need to approve a small customer credit for Brightline given 3+ hours of degraded UX while rolling mitigations. Suggested credit: 10% of this month's usage (we've modeled COA and revenue impact in the linked Jira).
2) Authorize a priority SRE/runtime post-incident task to harden chunk coalescing behavior and extend realtime trace retention to 72 hours for the affected pool. This requires extra logging budget; estimated cost ~$1,200/month for 3 months.
3) Approve a one-hour readiness call with Brightline CSM + Platform on Monday to run through our mitigation and confirm fallback paths.

Proposed next steps and timeline:
- Short (0–2h): monitor error rate and complete failover if error stays >1%
- Mid (2–24h): post-incident investigation and targeted fix for proxy->runtime reassembly logic
- Long (>24h): runtime change to make chunk coalescing robust under thread scheduling jitter

I'll run the incident postmortem and include action items. Happy to sync now if you prefer — otherwise I'll schedule the Monday readiness call after your sign-off.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
